messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@novacredit.com>, support@novacredit.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API — elevated response tail and partial throughput impact (notice)

Hi Elena / NovaCredit team,

Quick heads-up: between ~08:45 and 09:05 PT we observed elevated p95/p99 generation latencies and a small spike in 500 responses for a subset of requests routed to our hosted inference endpoints. The impact is partial — some customers and routes saw stretched tail latency (higher p99) and intermittent request failures; throughput for most customers remained within SLOs. We ran initial triage and want to surface what we know and recommended short-term actions.

What we saw (summary):
- Increased p95/p99 on generation endpoints, primarily on routes with long-sequence workloads.
- Brief spike in 500s correlating with a kernel selection fallback on a small subset of GPU hosts.
- Impact window: ~08:45–09:05 PT.

Immediate customer-facing mitigations we recommend:
- If you see transient failures, retry with exponential backoff (start 200ms).
- Prefer shorter max_tokens where possible during the window to reduce tail amplification.
- If you have a pinned model variant, consider switching to the earlier stable variant we offer (reply if you want us to flip this for you).

What we are doing:
- Ops has isolated the affected host pool and applied a kernel patch to eliminate the fallback condition.
- We’ve temporarily adjusted routing to favor dedicated pools where customers have capacity (no config change needed on your side).
- We’ll push an incident note to status.redwoodinference.com with live updates.

ETA for next update: 09:35 PT (we’ll confirm resolution or next steps). We’ll follow up with a short post-incident summary and a suggested set of long-term mitigations.

Attachments: investigation_timeline.pdf (PDF, 42KB) — short timeline and initial traces.

Apologies for the disruption — we’re prioritizing this and I’ll keep you posted. If you have immediate concerns or need specific logs/segments, reply and we’ll pull them.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — we saw the same behavior on our side (p99 jumps and ~2% 5xx increase) starting ~08:48. Our ingestion pipeline retried automatically and throttled some client-side downstream tasks.

Can you share the relevant traces for request ids 22f3a7 and 22f3a8 (we captured them)? Also please confirm whether the routing change affects any of our dedicated endpoints — we have strict isolation for certain workflows.

Appreciate the quick note.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T09:29:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API — elevated response tail and partial throughput impact (notice)

Ben — taking point on ops. Quick notes for the thread:
- Ops found the kernel-selection fallback triggered by an edge condition in our newer kernel on a small subset of hosts (3 nodes in us-west-2). That fallback increased latency under certain sequence-length distributions.
- We’ve removed the affected hosts from production rotation and rolled a hotfix to the kernel selection logic. Initial telemetry shows p99 dropping back to baseline.
- Routing change: we only shifted a very small fraction (~4% of affected traffic) to dedicated pools for customers with reservations; we did NOT touch strongly isolated dedicated endpoints. NovaCredit’s pinned/dedicated endpoints were not modified.

Action items
- Ben: share traces requested by NovaCredit (22f3a7 / 22f3a8) and the investigation_timeline.pdf.
- Vivek / Infra: confirm host remediation complete and provide post-fix telemetry.
- Laura: post a concise incident note to status page + Slack #customers-ops.

Marissa
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@novacredit.com>, support@novacredit.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API — elevated response tail and partial throughput impact (notice) — resolved + follow-up

Hi Elena — quick resolution note and next steps.

Status: Resolved at ~09:15 PT. The kernel-selection fallback triggered intermittent slow tails and a small number of 500s. We removed the three affected hosts and rolled a targeted kernel-selection patch; post-deploy telemetry shows p99 latency and error rates returned to baseline by 09:15.

Requested traces: attached pull for request ids 22f3a7 and 22f3a8 (included in investigation_timeline.pdf). If you need full request bodies/logs we can provide a redacted bundle via our secure transfer.

Postmortem (short):
- Root cause: an edge-case in the kernel selection path that caused fallbacks to a slower execution kernel under high sequence-length variance.
- Contributing factor: insufficient pre-release coverage on mixed-length workloads for the new kernel scheduler.
- Mitigations (short-term): removed affected hosts, hotfixed kernel selector, adjusted routing to avoid impacted host pool.
- Long-term actions: expand mixed-length workload tests in CI, add regression alerts on kernel-selector fallbacks, and include a canary ramp for kernel deployments.

We’ve started a postmortem draft and shared it to the drive: https://drive.redwoodinference.com/drive/folders/PM-DC-3948 (postmortem-draft.md attached). Expect a finalized postmortem by EOD tomorrow with clear timelines and preventive steps.

Apologies again for the disruption. If NovaCredit would like a short sync to review telemetry and the postmortem, I can schedule a 30-minute call later today or tomorrow morning.

Thanks for your patience — and please let us know if the traces don’t match what you captured.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
